messages:
maya: Heads up — we just got a support ticket: a customer on Dedicated reported that after their node went into maintenance and requests fell back to hosted, their dedicated burst credits were immediately drained. Looks like burst tokens didn’t 'freeze' on failover. Anyone seen this?

sam: Hmm. That sounds like our fallback routing keeps charging the request counter against the org's dedicated bucket even when served by hosted. I thought we had a check to avoid that. Can you paste the request ids?

maya: Sure. sample ids: req_e7a3, req_e7a4, req_e7a5. I also attached a snippet from quota logs: 

quota-bot: [LOG] 2026-12-06T14:02:11Z org=acme dedicated_bucket=org-42 consumed=+200 burst_remaining=0 fallback_route=hosted
quota-bot: [LOG] 2026-12-06T14:02:15Z org=acme hosted_route=us-west-2 served_by=hosted-2 request=req_e7a4

jihoon: That log implies our enforcement point (edge-proxy) uses the org->bucket mapping without checking runtime routing decisions. If the request is routed out, we should not decrement dedicated tokens. Could be a race: token pre-consumption at admission, route changes afterwards.

sam: Right — current flow: admit -> pre-consume tokens from bucket -> route -> if route fails we do fallback but we don't replenish tokens in all code paths. We added replenish only for explicit throttles, not for 'fallback to hosted'. Bug.

leah: From Product: customers expect that Dedicated reserved throughput is only charged when served by Dedicated hardware. If fallback to hosted still burns their reserved quota, that defeats the isolation guarantee. This is a big UX mismatch in Console.

noah: Observability note — console metrics are showing dedicated token usage decreasing even while dedicated GPU usage is zero during the maintenance window. That made the support triage confusing. We should add a telemetry label that indicates which enforcement path consumed the token (e.g., enforcement_source:pre-admit vs enforcement_source:post-route).

sam: Proposed short fix: when we pre-consume tokens we mark the pre-consume with a provisional flag and attach a unique admit_id. If route ends up outside dedicated (fallback), admission controller must call a 'release_preconsume(admit_id)'. I'll open a quick PR.

jihoon: Ok but we need to be careful for time windows: pre-consume -> long queue -> route success -> if release called too late we might artificially inflate available burst. Also think about burst_replenish_window semantics. Our token-bucket currently uses a large refill window (3600s) tuned for monthly billing patterns; for low-latency failovers we may want a per-second refill.

maya: The customer is sensitive to both availability and quota. They want guaranteed throughput while Dedicated is up, and not to lose credits just because we rerouted.

leah: Also Console should expose 'reserved vs consumed' separately per deployment mode. Right now we only surface a single "dedicated tokens consumed" metric. Need two: consumed_on_dedicated, consumed_on_hosted_fallback.

noah: Implementation note: add telemetry tag 'served_by_deployment_type' with values [dedicated, hosted, fallback_dedicated_policy] so billing and console can disambiguate. Also emit admit_id for tracing.

sam: Quick engineering trade: for safety we should prefer conservative revert-on-fallback — i.e., if route != dedicated then auto-replenish the provisional tokens immediately. But add a background reconcile job to catch edge races.

jihoon: Agree. For the refill algorithm, propose: switch default burst_replenish_window to token-bucket per-second refill (rate=burst_capacity/3600) but allow per-tenant override to a 'fast-recover' mode (for latency-critical customers) that refills within 60s. Need to map to pricing tiers though.

maya: Are there security/abuse implications if we allow fast-recover? Could a tenant spin many small failovers to game refill?

sam: It's possible. We should gate fast-recover behind higher tier SLA + audit logs. Also add a cooldown that limits how often refill mode can be toggled.

leah: Product asks: will this change affect existing reserved commitments? We need to update docs and show a 'what you paid for' explanation in Billing/Console.

noah: I'll add console instrumentation RFE: show real-time "effective throughput" split by deployment and a tooltip that explains provisional tokens and replenish behavior.

sam: I'll draft the PR with the pre-consume admit_id release path and an immediate replenish on fallback. Also adding metrics: quota.preconsume.admit_id, quota.released_on_fallback true/false.

jihoon: I'll take the refill policy change. Plan: default per-second refill, add tenant flag fast_refill=true with rate limiter. Will add unit tests around race conditions (preconsume -> concurrent release -> delayed success).

maya: Thanks. Can we also add a short incident annotation to the customer's audit log explaining root cause and that we credited back their burst? I'll coordinate with CS after the fix.

leah: Assign owners and milestone: sam -> enforcement fix (PR today), jihoon -> refill policy RFC (EOD), noah -> console telemetry patch (tomorrow). I'll open a follow-up RFC thread for policy and billing contract changes.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: sam/quicksync-preconsume-fix -> staging at 2026-12-06T15:10:00Z :rocket:

maya: Great — thanks all. Will patch CS and mark ticket: support-3821 as 'in progress'.

sam: One more: add an alert if dedicated token consumption increases while dedicated GPU utilization < 10% for 5m. That will catch this class of bug earlier.

noah: Added alert proposal to #eng-sre: "dedicated-quota-anomaly" with runbook to check routing table and preconsume traces.

maya: Closing loop: I'll confirm with customer once staging fix is validated. :thumbsup:
